figures.caption: Figure 1: FiQA examples of DESA (Maia et al., 2018; Thakur et al., 2021). Dense expansion recovers missing document semantics; sparse anchoring promotes jointly supported passages and excludes expansion-only matches. Two references are shown per query; text is abridged and paraphrased, and ranks use draw 0.

Table 2: Per-dataset evidence for channel-asymmetric construction. Effectiveness columns report relative nDCG@10 changes; +Dense and +Sparse compare DESA with the corresponding one-operator construction. Access columns report replay-depth reductions from Original, where positive values indicate shallower access. Sparse support is normalized by Original; red marks the sole degradation.

Table 4: Mechanism diagnostics computed from the frozen query constructions and rankings. Support retained is the mean per-query–draw fraction of the original sparse support; the displayed macro rounds to 100.0000%.

Table 5: Additional results. (a) Dataset-level controlled results. (b) Stratified paired tests after within-query averaging over three generation draws. (c) DESA query–draw sensitivity to fixed top-L, macro-averaged with equal dataset weight; exact top-20 compares with complete-list fusion, and the conclusion columns compare DESA with Original.
